uwp_capture_status: ok (with limitations): UWP app built (Release), deployed and launched — process HotspotApp (PID 56852), window 'Hotspot Authentication C# sample'. Scenario-1 golden captured live (real UI: Provision/Register enabled, Unregister disabled). uwp-app-runner returned ok:false at the verify stage ONLY because it searched for a process named after the csproj (HotspotAuthenticationApp) while the executable is HotspotApp.exe — no crash signature; the app was confirmed running. UWP behavioral baseline could not be captured: winapp UIA cannot descend into the UWP CoreWindow (ApplicationFrameHost-hosted) and the session is non-interactive (no foreground desktop), so scenarios 2/3 nav and all UWP control actuation could not be driven; goldens for 2/3 fell back to the scenario-1 frame.

features.name: Initialization
features.note: Structural coverage 3/3. WinUI control states match the UWP golden exactly: Provision=enabled, Register=enabled, Unregister=disabled. Register responds when invoked (+3 UIA text tokens). Provision invokes cleanly but is a no-op without signed WLAN provisioning XML (expected on a dev box).

features.name: Authentication by background task
features.note: Informational scenario with no interactive controls (coverage n/a). Reachable in WinUI; content (description + shared status area) present in the UIA tree.

features.name: Authentication by foreground app
features.note: Structural coverage 3/3 (Authenticate/Skip/Abort present). All three are disabled initially, matching the UWP source behavior (enabled only during a live NetworkOperatorHotspotAuthenticationContext event). Correctly hardware/event-gated, not dead controls.

measurement_notes.winui_screenshots_blank: WinUI 3 client-area screenshots render blank because the headless session's DWM does not composite the hardware-accelerated WinUI 3 surface into the captured bitmap. Grading relies on the fully-populated WinUI UIA tree (correct geometry + enabled/disabled states), which matches the UWP checklist and scenario-1 golden.
